items.text: **Tempo now comes back down.** Raising the tempo quickly and then setting it back to 20 left the music (and held notes) running fast, because the slow glide to the new tempo took its wobble from wherever the glide had got to. The wobble is now fixed once per pass, so the tempo always lands on the slider.

**Redo no longer meets the tempo bar.** On an iPad in landscape at about 900 to 1000 px the tempo bar was squeezed until its speaker, metronome and slider piled up beside undo and redo. It now keeps a minimum width and the bar wraps to a second line when there is not room.

recording a held note is easier. **Press and hold the note still for half a second** (a small buzz) to start a take, or tap its circle. While it records, **a touch anywhere on the pad** controls that note, so your finger can't miss it or hold other cells. **Lifting your finger** ends the take and loops it. (The circle itself is smaller, and sits at the top middle of a narrow cell.)
Changed: the line-up button no longer shows three bars when the line-up is custom; it shows a broken-lines icon, since three bars read as a menu or "off".
Changed: the Swell button now tells the browser not to take over the touch for scrolling while it is held.

on a device that reports pressure (an Apple Pencil), pressing harder on a held note sets its level and brightness, and hold record captures it. A finger on an iPad does not report pressure, so there the vertical drag still sets the level.
Fixed: 0.9.32 and 0.9.33 shipped with a stray bracket that stopped the page starting. This release repairs it; the icons and wave from 0.9.32 are in it.

**hold record**. In the hold hand, each held note shows a small empty circle at its top right. Tap it to record what you do to that note (its level and its reverb), tap again to loop that move in time with the tempo, tap once more to stop the loop. Dragging the note or letting it go ends the loop.

the page now tells iPadOS its app name (Battanboo) and that it is a full-screen web app, so the window switcher can show the name instead of "Web". Add it to the Home Screen again after this update to pick it up.

Changed: the index icons are now one each. **The field** wears its real cube; **The lines** is a stepped line walking across the grid (it no longer looks like Settings); **Settings** is a gear; **Install**, **Before you perform** and **Self-test** have their own icons instead of borrowing the cloud and the compass.
Changed: **Swell** drops the shoreline; a second small curl follows the wave below its crest.
Changed: in The grid, switches (normal, muted, always on) and locks (open, locked) are shown as pictures with a few words each, instead of paragraphs.

Fixed: on a slider with a morph set (for example "Repeat the step before"), the two little range dots sat on the label instead of on the track, because they were placed while the section was still closed. They now follow the slider whenever it appears or changes size.

accessibility is now a rule for every feature, and this release is the first sweep. The page declares its language and a main area, decorative pictures are hidden from screen readers, no two elements share an id any more (the Hidden-controls rows and the bar's icon copies did), and real messages are read out through a polite announcer instead of the every-frame status line.
Changed: with "reduce motion" on in your device, the full-screen equalizer shows its plain bar instead of moving.
Known gap: the score grid itself cannot yet be played or edited from a keyboard. That is the next building step.
